146.h: 51 - Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays ibn Maʿbad (3) ibn al-Ḥārith al-Khathʿamiyyah * (ع)
t: Umm ʿAbd Allāh. ⟦2:282⟧
Among the first female emigrants.

It is said: she accepted Islam before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the House of al-Arqam (1), and her husband Jaʿfar al-Ṭayyār emigrated with her to Abyssinia, where she bore him: ʿAbd Allāh, Muḥammad and ʿAwn.

When she emigrated with him to Medina in the year 7, and he was martyred on the day of Mūtah, Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq married her, and she bore him Muḥammad at the time of ihram; she then performed the Farewell Pilgrimage. Then al-Ṣiddīq died and she washed him (2), and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib married her.
سفيان بن عيينة: عن إسماعيل، عن الشعبي، قال:
Asmāʾ arrived from Abyssinia, and ʿUmar said to her: O Abyssinian woman, we preceded you in emigration.

She said: By my life, you have spoken the truth. You were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who fed your hungry and taught your ignorant, while we were the distant ones, the driven away. By Allah, I will certainly mention that to the Messenger of Allah.
She came to him, and he said: (The people have one emigration, and you have two emigrations) (3). ⟦2:283⟧
عبد الله بن نمير: عن الأجلح، عن عامر، قال:
Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays said: O Messenger of Allah! These people claim that we are not among the emigrants.
He said: (He lies who says that; you have the emigration twice: you emigrated to the Negus, and you emigrated to me (1)).
al-Shaʿbī said: The first to recommend a bier for a woman - meaning the covered litter - was Asmāʾ; she saw the Christians make it in Abyssinia (2).
الحكم بن عتيبة (3) : عن عبد الله بن شداد، عن أسماء بنت عميس، قالت:
When Jaʿfar was struck down, he said: Put on mourning dress (4) for three days, then do as you wish (5). ⟦2:284⟧

Ibn al-Musayyab said: Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays gave birth (1) to Muḥammad at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, as they were setting out for the Farewell Pilgrimage, and Abū Bakr ordered her to wash, and then to enter ihram for the Hajj (2).
الثوري: عن عبد الكريم، عن سعيد بن المسيب، قال:
She gave birth at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, and Abū Bakr thought of sending her back, so he asked the Prophet ﷺ, who said: (Order her to wash, then enter ihram for the Hajj (3)).
al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad narrated from Asmāʾ something similar to it.
ابن سعد: أخبرنا يزيد، أخبرنا ابن أبي خالد، عن قيس، قال:
I entered with Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) - he was fair-skinned and light of flesh - and I saw Asmāʾ's hands tattooed.
Added: خالد الطحان، عن إسماعيل، عن قيس: she used to defend Abū Bakr (4). ⟦2:285⟧
Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, judge (القاضي) of Medina, said: Abū Bakr left a bequest that Asmāʾ should wash him.
Qatādah said: Bint ʿUmays, his wife, washed him (1).
It is said: he had urged her, when she was fasting, to break her fast, and said: It is stronger for you.
She remembered his oath at the end of the day, called for water, drank, and said: By Allah, I will not follow him with a broken oath today (2).
Mālik narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr:
That Asmāʾ washed Abū Bakr, and asked those of the emigrants who were present, saying: I am fasting, and this is a very cold day; must I perform a ritual wash?
They said: No (3).
Abū Isḥāq narrated from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd:
That ʿUmar fixed the stipends, and fixed for Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays a thousand dirhams (4).
al-Wāqidī said: Then she married ʿAlī, and bore him: Yaḥyā and ʿAwn (5).
Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah said: I heard ʿĀmir say:

ʿAlī married Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays, and her two sons, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, boasted against each other; each of them said: I am nobler than you, and my father is better than your father.
He said: ʿAlī said to her: Judge between them.
She said: I have not seen a young man of the Arabs better than Jaʿfar, nor an older man better than Abū Bakr. ⟦2:286⟧
ʿAlī said: You have left nothing for us; had you said other than what you said, I would have hated you.
She said: Three men, of whom you are the lowest, are the best (1).
ابن عيينة: عن إسماعيل، عن قيس، قال:
ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Among women, al-Ḥāriqah (2) lied to you, and no woman of them stood firm except Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays.
I say: Asmāʾ has a hadith in the Sunan collections (السنن) of the Four.
Narrating from her: ابنها؛ عبد الله بن جعفر، وابن أختها؛ عبد الله بن شداد، وسعيد بن المسيب، وعروة، والشعبي، والقاسم بن محمد، وآخرون.
She lived after ʿAlī.
